I'm Eric, and I graduated in 2024 from Harvard. I currently live in New York City. 

I'm not currently seeking new opportunities, but do enjoy getting in touch. If you'd like to send me a message, please do so with a *bad running-related pun*.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
• Used Ruby and Elasticsearch to build on Stripe’s Public Search API, by adding support for new query fields, impacting endpoints called over 1M times per day to access petabytes of payment data.
• Led a cross-functional effort to construct a platform for Stripe-wide Java services to make Elasticsearch queries. Designed and implemented a Java client library for handling queries based on feedback from Accounts and Security teams.
• Built and deployed a new gRPC microservice in Go to act as a proxy for client library requests, handling calls to Elasticsearch APIs and enforcing authorization checks based on internal context-aware datastore access libraries.

positions.title: Director of Events
positions.description:
Harvard Computer Society (HCS) represents a community of undergraduate and graduate students at Harvard interested in tech and computer science.
• Partnered with sponsors and other student organizations to host multiple club events per semester, such as expert panels, coffee chats, and coding competitions.
• Managed email messages for mailing list of 400+ members.

positions.title: Student Developer
positions.description:
Served remotely as a student developer within the bank's technology division.
• Led the redesign of a legacy invoice management website, allowing users to execute CRUD operations on invoice record data, filter and download data, and trigger stored procedures and ETL processes on a SQL Server database. Created backend in Go and developed an updated UI with user authentication using Angular and Angular Material components.
• Contributed to and tested Go backend for a CSV file validation web app used in an internal fraud detection project.
• Managed project workflows on GitHub, and documented project codebases. Wrote guides for setting up development software and installing npm and Angular in corporate environments for team members.

positions.title: Academic Tutor
positions.description:
Worked with Olympiads School, a business that provides academic and contest preparation courses, as a tutor for summer session classes.
• Organized weekly tutorial sessions for students taking Grade 11/12 chemistry courses, explaining concepts and solving example problems.
• Presented a seminar about the college application process.

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description:
Ivy Path School is an extracurricular business that offers preparatory courses for students in the Greater Toronto Area.
• Wrote class handouts and problem sets and taught weekly lessons for a contest chemistry class, covering concepts for the Avogadro and Chem 13 News contests, as well as the Canadian Chemistry Contest/Olympiad.
• Organized and taught an online IB Higher Level Chemistry crash course, creating presentations and homework while corresponding with students virtually.

positions.title: President
positions.description:
Youth Nation Alliance (YNA) is a student-led non-profit organization that connects high school youth with volunteering opportunities. YNA has built up a volunteering base of 1700+ members, and partnered with municipal governments. YNA also works with local youth organizations and community groups to offer volunteering events and share leadership opportunities.
• Wrote material for the organization's website and sponsorship booklets; directed grant applications.
• Organized executive meetings and socials to discuss updates and organization development.
• Corresponded with the City of Richmond Hill and other non-profits to find, plan logistics for, and coordinate upcoming volunteering events.
• Managed social media campaigns promoting YNA.
• Recruited and directed orientation for incoming executives for future years.
A special initiative, planned in conjunction with the Markham Mayor's Youth Council, was the Markham Youth Civic Action Initiative 2019, introducing dozens of students to principles of political engagement through a mock city hall and debate session. This event was made possible by a community grant from the Laidlaw Foundation.

positions.title: Co-Chair - Richmond Hill's Youth Action Committee
positions.description:
The Youth Action Committee serves as an advisory council for the Parks and Recreation Department of the Town of Richmond Hill. The Committee plans several events around the Town throughout the year, and works with the Town to give a youth's perspective on municipal affairs.
• Directed Committee executives and collaborated with City staff to oversee marketing, logistics, and sponsorship efforts for all events.
• Planned and hosted Committee meetings and event preparation.
• Managed member recruitment and executive selection.
• Represented 25,000+ teen voices in the City of Richmond Hill at municipal parades, ward festivals, and city council meetings.

positions.title: Marketing Director - Richmond Hill's Youth Action Committee
positions.description:
• Sought sponsorships from various businesses in Richmond Hill for the Committee.
• Designed and wrote event programmes and graphic materials for participants, collaborating with executives to revise designs and gain/give feedback.
• Managed organization's social media presence to promote YAC events and recruitment.

positions.title: Marketing Executive - Richmond Hill's Youth Action Committee
Laboratory Assistant
positions.description:
Served as a lab assistant within the Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry, helping graduate students with research projects.
• Constructed PDMS microfluidic devices and used a pressure controller and syringe pump to observe the behaviour of water droplets in a flow of mineral oil, analyzing data in MATLAB to calculate interfacial tension values.
• Assisted in pH calculations and neutralizations for Greiss-like coupling reactions using gold nanoparticles (AuNPs).
• Took and measured contact angles of silicone oil on PDMS substrates using a high-speed camera.
• Summarized and presented results in weekly meetings to research group.

positions.title: SHAD Fellow
positions.description:
SHAD is a Canada-wide, month-long summer program that focuses on science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics. I attended the SHAD 2018 program at the University of Prince Edward Island. 
• Edited and designed program "monthbook"
• Placed second overall at the program's Design challenge, a pitch competition for products/services helping communities improve resilience against natural disasters

projects.title: Scantry
projects.description: Scantry was a project created at ECHacks 2018 which allows users to automatically catalog groceries by scanning them with a mobile device. It uses Clarifai's Machine Vision API on a mobile app created with Expo.io to recognize pictures of food items. This data is then pushed to Firebase, where it can be accessed online via a website created with Netlify.

projects.title: FoodWatch
projects.description:
FoodWatch was a project created for PennApps XVIII at the University of Pennsylvania in September 2018. The premise of the project was to reduce food waste by giving users an accessible catalog of what they have in their fridge. 

FoodWatch operates via SMS messages between the user and the platform using Twilio. To add items to their inventory (the groceries they currently have), the user provides a description and expiry date. To view their inventory, the user may send a message, and is returned with a full list of items and their expiry dates. In addition, the user may also view their list or remove items online. Data is hosted on Google's Firebase platform, and a Flask framework was used for frontend.

testScores.name: IB Diploma Program
testScores.description:
One of 141 Diploma candidates out of a candidate pool of 170,000+ to receive a full score on the IB Diploma. 

Subjects: 
• Higher Level Chemistry: 7
• Higher Level History of Europe: 7
• Higher Level English Literature: 7
• Standard Level Mathematics: 7
• Standard Level Physics: 7
• Standard Level French B: 7
• Extended Essay: A
• Theory of Knowledge: B

organizations.name: DECA Ontario
organizations.position: Masters' Club, Innovators' Council · Nov 2017 - May 2019
organizations.description:
The Masters' Club is a collection of students within DECA Ontario who write articles to help members prepare for their competitive events at the International Career Development Conference. I served in this position from November 2017 to February 2018.
- Wrote a series of articles and graphic aids for competitors in the Principles oral presentation categories in preparation for the International Career Development Conference 2018
- Collaborated with other students in the Club and the Provincial Officers to edit and revise articles.

Additionally, from October 2018 to May 2019, I served on the Innovators' Council, where I collaborated with individuals to:
- Seek sponsorships from local businesses for the 2019 provincial competition
- Design and implement a photo contest for competitors at the 2019 provincial competition

organizations.name: STEM Fellowship
organizations.description:
STEM Fellowship is a Canada-wide network of students interested in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. The Fellowship has organized national contests such as the Big Data Challenge and the Canadian Young Physicists' Tournament (CaYPT) 2017.
- Provided feedback on Fellowship events and programs
- Boosted Fellowship outreach on Facebook
